content.value_statement: Modern Android UI work needs consistent Compose patterns. This skill guides state, navigation, Material 3, and performance choices for production screens.
actual_capabilities: Outlines Compose BOM and dependency setup for Gradle version catalogs.
Shows ViewModel and StateFlow patterns for UI state.
Demonstrates state hoisting from screen composables to stateless content.
Provides type-safe Navigation Compose examples with serializable destinations.
Lists performance practices for remember, derivedStateOf, stability, and side effects.
limitations: Does not run Android builds, tests, or device checks.
Example dependency versions may need updates for current projects.
Does not provide full migration plans for every XML layout pattern.
Assumes the user already has a Kotlin Android project context.

use_cases.title: New Compose Feature
use_cases.description: Create a screen structure with state, content, loading, error, and retry handling.

use_cases.title: Architecture Review
use_cases.description: Review Compose state ownership, ViewModel boundaries, and callback flow before implementation.

use_cases.title: Navigation Upgrade
use_cases.description: Plan typed Navigation Compose routes and argument handling for existing screens.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a simple Jetpack Compose screen for [feature]. Include state fields, loading, error, and success UI.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor State Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Compose screen and ViewModel. Suggest an MVI or MVVM state model using StateFlow and clear event callbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Type-Safe Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a type-safe Navigation Compose flow for [app area]. Include destinations, arguments, screen ownership, and state boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Compose Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Compose UI for unnecessary recomposition. Recommend remember, derivedStateOf, stable models, and side-effect changes.

output_examples.input: I need a Compose profile screen with loading, errors, and retry.
output: A screen state model with loading, user, and error fields.
A ViewModel plan that exposes immutable StateFlow.
A composable structure that separates screen wiring from stateless content.

output_examples.input: Review my Compose navigation plan for profile and settings screens.
output: Typed destination recommendations for each screen.
Argument ownership guidance for route data.
A note about keeping navigation outside child UI components.

output_examples.input: Find likely recomposition problems in this dashboard UI.
output: A prioritized performance review of state reads and derived calculations.
Suggestions for remember, derivedStateOf, and stable UI models.
Testing notes for Layout Inspector and recomposition checks.

best_practices: Provide the current screen, state model, and navigation requirements.
Ask for state ownership and side-effect guidance before adding complex UI behavior.
Validate generated patterns with Android Studio, tests, and device checks.
anti_patterns: Requesting UI code without project constraints, dependencies, or architecture choices.
Treating example dependency versions as guaranteed current for every project.
Passing ViewModels through every composable instead of using state and callbacks.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete Android apps?
faq.answer: No. It guides Compose architecture and examples, but you must integrate and test the code.

faq.question: Can it help with Material Design 3?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Material 3 screen structure and component choices in Compose.

faq.question: Does it support Navigation Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes type-safe navigation patterns and route argument guidance.

faq.question: Can it optimize recomposition?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review state, remember usage, stability, and side effects for common performance issues.

faq.question: Does it replace Android testing?
faq.answer: No. You still need unit, UI, and device testing for your app.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
